headline: What Amazon already collects, keeps, and shares about you.
subhead: The policy you agreed to by using Amazon — explained plainly.
changes: In-store cameras, sensors, and computer vision track your physical movements and product interactions.
Amazon shares your advertising identifier and ad-value estimates with ad companies, who may then use it to target you for other advertisers.
In a sale or acquisition, your personal data transfers to the new owner as a business asset.
When you update personal info, Amazon keeps a copy of the old version in its records — indefinitely.
verdict_text: Most practices here are industry-standard. The physical store surveillance and the ad-value data sharing with third-party ad networks are the details most users would not expect.
actions: Visit Your Ads Privacy Choices at amazon.com to limit ad targeting.
Go to Data Privacy Queries to request access to or deletion of your data.
Review and edit your browsing history at amazon.com/gp/history to reduce recommendation tracking.

categories.explanation: Amazon shares your advertising identifier and an estimate of your ad value with external ad companies, who may use it to serve you ads from other advertisers entirely.
When you update personal information such as your address or profile details, Amazon retains a copy of the previous version in its records with no stated time limit.
Amazon's physical stores use cameras, computer vision, and sensors to record your movements and which products you interact with while shopping in person.

headline: What Amazon's terms already let them do with your content
subhead: Reviews, posts, and content you submit belong to Amazon forever.
changes: Any review or photo you post grants Amazon a permanent, royalty-free, worldwide license.
That license is irrevocable and sublicensable - Amazon can pass your content to others.
Disputes go to King County, Washington courts only - jury trial waived by both sides.
App permissions for Amazon apps are acknowledged but details are not listed in this document.
verdict_text: The perpetual content license and jury-trial waiver are standard in big-tech terms but broader than most users realize. No evidence of data sale in these excerpts.
actions: Avoid posting original creative content in Amazon reviews.
Note that disputes must be filed in Washington state courts, not locally.
Check Amazon's separate app permissions page before installing Amazon apps.

categories.explanation: You agreed that any dispute with Amazon must be settled in Washington state courts and that neither side gets a jury trial.
Amazon apps request device permissions, but the actual list of those permissions is not described in this document - only linked externally.

headline: WhatsApp just updated its privacy policy
subhead: A video selfie may be involved. Here's the TL;DR
changes: A third-party service can now estimate your age from a video selfie

actions: Set a username when it rolls out — stop sharing your number
Review Settings → Privacy: who sees your photo and info
Read the full policy and the exact changes — link in bio

headline: You can opt out of Price Plus data sharing. It says that may cost you deals.
changes: Price Plus links your name, address, phone and purchase history

actions: Opt out of sharing at 1-800-SHOPRITE or customer service
Keep the card for product recall alerts
NJ residents can request their data under NJDPA

categories.explanation: Policy describes sharing personal information with engaged third parties and states that opting out may disqualify members from promotions requiring individual-level data.

headline: 63 million loyalty members. One income predictor. It can be wrong.

actions: Ask Kroger to correct your shopper profile
Request your data - many states now guarantee access
Check advertised shelf prices against your receipt

categories.explanation: Consumer Reports reported one loyalty profile may have been shared with more than 50 U.S. companies including data brokers, tobacco companies and financial institutions.

headline: Its limits on how partners use your data carve out advertising.
changes: Contract limits on data sharing exclude some advertising uses
Best Buy says it doesn't trade your data for money
It still lists data sold under New Jersey's broader definition
Joining My Best Buy requires name, address, email and phone

actions: Use Best Buy's advertising opt-out on its privacy page
Cancel membership by phone: 1-888-237-8289
Opting out cannot legally get you worse treatment

categories.explanation: Policy states the general contractual limits on recipient use do not apply to some sharing for advertising purposes, including cross-context behavioral advertising.

headline: Owner of ACME and Kings. It values your loyalty data at $4.13 a shopper.
changes: Albertsons estimates your data is worth about $4.13 per shopper
Cameras may infer race, religion, and disability as demographic data
Loyalty data is an enumerated input for training AI models
Store Wi-Fi ties your device ID and location to your account

actions: Delete shopping history only - keeps your account and points
Opt out of sale and targeted ads: (877) 251-6559
Turn on Global Privacy Control in your browser

categories.explanation: Policy discloses sharing identifiers, device data, geolocation, loyalty information and commercial data with advertisers, ad tech companies, marketing platforms and data analytics providers.
Data Use section lists training artificial intelligence or machine learning models, including those provided by service providers, as an enumerated purpose.

headline: Amazon now uses your data to train AI
subhead: New generative AI clause added to privacy policy.
changes: Amazon now explicitly uses your data to develop and deploy generative AI models.
Linking your Amazon account to a third-party via Login with Amazon is now listed as a data source.
Amazon replaced 'search results and Sponsored Links' with broader ad-interaction tracking on third-party sites and apps.
Amazon now collects advertising identifiers and data from third parties to improve its services.
verdict_text: The new AI training clause and expanded ad-tracking language meaningfully broaden how Amazon can use your personal data.
actions: Review Amazon's Generative AI Development Disclosure linked in the policy.
Check your ad preferences and opt out of interest-based ads at amazon.com/ibanotice.
Avoid linking your Amazon account to third-party apps unless necessary.

categories.explanation: Amazon added explicit language stating it uses customer data, including browsing and purchase behavior, to develop and deploy its generative AI models and services.
Amazon replaced a narrow reference to sponsored search links with broader language about collecting ad-interaction data and advertising identifiers from third-party websites and apps.

headline: Telegram expands how it targets ads to you
subhead: Your location and followed channels now shape ads.
changes: Ad-free pledge narrowed: only chat contents and contact lists are protected.
Ads can now be targeted by country or city, estimated from your phone number or IP.
Channels you follow can determine which ad categories you see across Telegram.
Ads now run in bots, stories, and public search — not just large channels.
verdict_text: Telegram's privacy promise got narrower. Location-based and interest-based ad targeting is now explicit, though no data is passed to advertisers.
actions: Check Settings > Privacy & Security > Data Settings to limit ad data.
Consider Telegram Premium if you want to opt out of all ads.
Review which public channels you follow, as they now influence ad targeting.

categories.explanation: The updated policy clarifies that location estimates derived from phone number area codes or IP addresses are used for ad targeting, though Telegram states this data is never passed directly to advertisers.
Telegram now explicitly uses IP address and phone number area code to approximate a user's country and city for ad-targeting purposes, a previously undisclosed use of this data.

headline: Facebook rewrote its privacy policy structure
subhead: Bigger, more detailed — but what actually changed for you?
changes: Meta now explicitly lists publicly available datasets used to improve AI and ML models.
New section details data collected when you interact with Meta's generative AI features.
Policy now spells out cross-account data combining when WhatsApp is linked via Accounts Center.
Expanded detail on third-party data sources: data brokers, marketing vendors, academic institutions.
verdict_text: The restructured policy surfaces AI training and cross-app data merging more explicitly, giving users clearer — but broader — disclosure of how their data is used.
actions: Review your Accounts Center to see which Meta apps share your data.
Check 'Off-Facebook Activity' settings to limit third-party data flowing in.
Audit your AI feature interactions and connected third-party apps in Facebook settings.

categories.explanation: The updated policy explicitly states that publicly available datasets from data providers and research institutions are used to improve Meta's AI and ML technologies, including natural language processing and computer vision.

The policy now provides an expanded and explicit list of third-party sources supplying user data to Meta, including marketing and advertising vendors, data providers, industry peers, and public institutions.

headline: Robinhood updated its privacy policy for AI
subhead: AI agents can now interact with your account and data
changes: Robinhood now collects your data when external AI agents use its services on your behalf.
Third-party AI agents can connect to your account like Google or Apple sign-in.
Robinhood Ventures Fund II replaces Fund I across affiliate data-sharing notices.
A new Customer Agreement covers 'agentic trading' by external AI on your account.
verdict_text: AI agents accessing your financial account is a meaningful new data-collection scenario ordinary users should understand before enabling.
actions: Check if any third-party AI tools are connected to your Robinhood account.
Review the updated Customer Agreement for agentic trading rules.
Revisit your GLBA affiliate-sharing opt-out under the updated entity list.

categories.explanation: Robinhood already had AI training language, but now explicitly includes data generated when external AI agents use your account as potential training input.
Third-party AI agents are newly named alongside Google and Apple as external services that can connect to your account and share your profile data with Robinhood.

headline: Flock just changed its surveillance rules
subhead: The license plate camera network cut how long it stores your movements — with a catch.
changes: Default data retention drops from 30 days to 7 days.
But existing agencies keep their current period unless they opt in.
Cities can now block outside agencies from searching their cameras for immigration enforcement.
Misuse detection becomes mandatory for all police customers by the end of 2026.
Abnormal search patterns will trigger an automatic lockout pending administrator review.
Every search will require a case number, and multi-factor login is now mandatory.
verdict_text: The audit requirements are real. But the 7-day retention is a recommendation, not a switch. How long your movements are stored still depends on your city council, not on Flock.
actions: Look up your police department's Flock Transparency Portal.
Ask your city council: 7-day retention, or still 30?
Check deflock.org for cameras mapped near you.

headline: Amazon now requires arbitration, drops jury trials
subhead: Big dispute-resolution overhaul affects every US shopper.
changes: Disputes must now go to binding arbitration, not court
Class-action lawsuits against Amazon are now banned
You must contact customer service and wait 60 days before arbitrating
Personal injury claims from products now governed by your state's law
verdict_text: Amazon replaced a simple court clause with extensive mandatory arbitration and a class-action waiver, significantly limiting how users can seek legal relief.
actions: Read the new arbitration section at amazon.com/conditions
Note the 60-day pre-arbitration step before filing any claim
For product-injury claims, check which state law applies to you

categories.explanation: Amazon replaced a simple court-jurisdiction clause with extensive mandatory binding arbitration and an explicit class-action waiver, removing users' right to jury trials and collective legal action.

key_changes: Alexa now called out specifically:** The service terms intro now explicitly names Alexa (and links to its Terms of Use) as a service with additional terms, where it previously was not listed. This appears to be a transparency update, though it signals Amazon wants users clearly bound by Alexa-specific terms.

headline: Twitch now uses your data to train AI
subhead: Your activity feeds Twitch and Amazon's generative AI.
changes: Twitch explicitly added AI and machine learning training as a use of your data.

This applies across Twitch products and Amazon's broader services ecosystem.
A link to Amazon's Generative AI Disclosure was added for more detail.
verdict_text: Twitch has explicitly added AI training — including generative AI — as a permitted use of all user data, with no opt-out mentioned in the diff.
actions: Visit Twitch's Privacy Choices page to review your current data options.
Check Amazon's Generative AI Development Disclosure linked in the policy.
Consider what activity you share publicly on Twitch going forward.

categories.explanation: Twitch added explicit language permitting user data to be used for machine learning and generative AI model development across Twitch and Amazon's products, a use not previously stated in the policy.

headline: Steam quietly swapped its EU privacy contact

No action needed if you are outside the EU or have no active requests.

Review My AI chat history and delete anything you don't want used for training.
Visit Snapchat's Privacy Center to audit what data Snap holds about you.

categories.explanation: The updated policy clarifies that content shared with My AI, including text, images, and location, is used as input to generate outputs and improve AI model responses, making the AI training use more explicit than before.

Snapchat added new language allowing it to use face detection information from your Memories for grouping, search, and personalisation features, representing an expanded use of biometric-adjacent data from your camera roll.

Follow @tos_monitor for alerts if substantive changes appear

headline: Instagram tightens rules on automated data collection
subhead: New terms govern bots, scrapers, and data harvesting
changes: Automated scraping now governed by a formal 'Automated Data Collection Terms' document
Instagram can revoke permission for any automated data collection at any time
Bots and scrapers must comply with the new terms even if previously allowed
Clarifies that automated access rules apply whether or not you're logged in
verdict_text: This formalises and expands restrictions on scraping and bots, and gives Instagram broader power to revoke access without notice.
actions: If you use any automation tools on Instagram, review the new Automated Data Collection Terms
Developers or businesses using the API should audit their current data practices now
Regular users: no action needed, but know Instagram is cracking down on scrapers
key_changes: Instagram now explicitly links its ban on unauthorized automated data collection to a separate **"Automated Data Collection Terms"** document, which appears to define what counts as "Automated Data Collection" — users (and especially developers/scrapers) are now bound by that additional policy

The updated text now states that Instagram **"may restrict or revoke our permission at any time"** for any automated access — making it clearer that any permission granted is not guaranteed or permanent

This change primarily targets scrapers, bots, and third-party tools, but could also affect **everyday users who rely on third-party apps** that pull Instagram data (e.g., scheduling tools, analytics apps), if those tools lose permission
